topic:
Organizing a Cluttered Space  
Useful expressions: "clear out," "sort through," "donate unused items."
script: Hey everyone, welcome to "Chillwave B2".
I'm Ethan.
Today, let’s chat about clearing out that clutter we all accumulate.
I ran into a friend last week who was totally stressed about their messy apartment.
So, grab a drink, get comfortable, and let’s sort through some solutions together.

Heh, I had this old bookshelf in my room that was just overflowing with stuff I didn’t even use anymore. It was like a time capsule—half the stuff had been there since high school. So I finally said, "Enough is enough," and started to clear out the clutter. I sorted through everything, pulled out the books I wanted to keep, and set aside the rest. A lot of it was just old clothes or broken headphones I could barely remember owning. I ended up donating a bunch of unused items, and now the room actually feels like it breathes.
Did you ever find something unexpected while cleaning out your space?
I had this drawer under my desk that was basically a mystery—I hadn’t opened it in years.
Turns out, it was full of old pens, empty wrappers, and even a mix tape from 2012.
Clearing it out made me realize how much little junk we hold on to without a second thought.
After I sorted through everything, I actually found a few things I didn’t want to part with.
But most of it? I dropped off with some other unused stuff at a local thrift store yesterday.
What’s the weirdest thing you’ve pulled out while cleaning up your clutter?
I mean, it’s funny how something small can take up so much mental space just by sitting there ignored.
Sometimes just starting is the hardest part, right?
Once you get going, it’s like all this weight lifts off your shoulders.
Take your time with it—there’s no rush to clear everything in one night.
And if you find something that makes you smile, like me with that mix tape, hold onto it.
But if it’s just taking up room, maybe pass it on to someone who can use it.
So here’s a little tip that helped me out—use the “one in, one out” rule when organizing.
I noticed that every time I bought something new, I’d just add to the mess without thinking.
The idea is to remove an old item before bringing in a new one, so your space stays balanced.
It works for clothes, books, even your phone downloads!
Honestly, it keeps me from getting carried away and piling up more clutter.
Well, organizing doesn’t have to be a chore—just start with one corner or one box and work your way up.
If it hasn’t brought you joy in a while, maybe it’s time to clear it out and make space for something new.
Thanks for sticking around and cleaning up your space with me tonight.
Heh, take care and don’t let the clutter get too comfy, okay? Goodnight!
